title: Useful speculative transfers did not establish downstream benefit
summary: The three-seed reference experiment selected a nonreturning source and wasted speculative traffic. A disjoint trace consumed every staged byte but only tied demand controls in executed prompt work and took more model-runner time.
scope: 40 accepted cells and 1,944 exact requests overall. The reference supplement has three seeds on one input cohort; the disjoint supplement has one independent trace.
limitations: Current-stream instrumented GPU timings are not uninstrumented production cost. The disjoint trace has no uncertainty interval. This rejects the tested release claim, not every possible semantic predictor.
decision: Keep the negative result and require evidence of saved work or useful latency before interpreting transfer activation as benefit.

chart.caption: Higher is slower. Reference interval is the original small-sample normal approximation; the disjoint point has no interval.
